title: The Cyrillic alphabet: 33 letters
explanation: Some letters are "false friends" of Latin (В=v, Н=n, Р=r, С=s, У=u, Х=kh).
bridge_note: both scripts descend from Greek, so shapes overlap but sound-values diverged.
branch: Cyrillic Alphabet, Sound System, and Reading (Prerequisite Unit)

title: Vowels: hard-series vs soft-series (а/я, о/ё, у/ю, э/е, ы/и)
explanation: The "soft" vowel letters signal palatalization of the preceding consonant.

examples.gloss: hard vs. soft "m" before the vowel (а vs я)
onion / manhole — same hard/soft pattern with у vs ю

bridge_note: the two series encode consonant softness in the vowel letter.
branch: Cyrillic Alphabet, Sound System, and Reading (Prerequisite Unit)

title: The soft sign ь and hard sign ъ
explanation: ь palatalizes and has no sound of its own; ъ is a rare separator.
bridge_note: ь is a fossil of a once-pronounced ultra-short vowel (jer).
branch: Cyrillic Alphabet, Sound System, and Reading (Prerequisite Unit)

title: Voiced/voiceless pairs and final devoicing
explanation: год sounds like "got"; друг → "druk".

examples.gloss: year, friend — final voiced consonants devoice: sound like "got", "druk"

mistake: pronouncing final voiced consonants as in English.
branch: Cyrillic Alphabet, Sound System, and Reading (Prerequisite Unit)

title: Word stress and vowel reduction (акание)
explanation: Unstressed о reduces to an "a"-like sound; stress is unpredictable and mobile.
bridge_note: Russian is stress-timed with strong reduction.
branch: Cyrillic Alphabet, Sound System, and Reading (Prerequisite Unit)

title: Intonation contours ИК-1 to ИК-5
explanation: Pitch, not word order, distinguishes a statement (ИК-1) from a yes/no question (ИК-3). Example: Это Анна. vs Это Анна?

examples.gloss: Is this Anna? (rising pitch, ИК-3 — same words)

branch: Cyrillic Alphabet, Sound System, and Reading (Prerequisite Unit)

title: Noun gender from the ending
explanation: Consonant/-й → m (стол, музей); -а/-я → f (книга, неделя); -о/-е → n (окно, море).
bridge_note: gender is agreement machinery, largely divorced from sex, surviving from PIE.
branch: The Bones of the Simple Sentence: Gender, "to be", and "to have"

title: The soft-sign gender ambiguity (-ь nouns)
explanation: Nouns in -ь are masculine OR feminine and must be learned individually; roughly two-thirds are feminine. Signposts: -ость always f (радость, новость); -тель, -арь m (учитель, словарь); days/months m (день, январь); -чь/-щь tend f (ночь, вещь).
bridge_note: these descend from an old i-stem declension that merged endings.
mistake: guessing feminine every time; forgetting gender governs agreement (Дверь была открыта).
branch: The Bones of the Simple Sentence: Gender, "to be", and "to have"

title: No present-tense "to be": the zero copula
explanation: Russian omits "is" in the present; "X is Y" is "X — Y".
bridge_note: the old present forms of быть fell out of use, leaving a gap English speakers keep filling.
branch: The Bones of the Simple Sentence: Gender, "to be", and "to have"

title: Possession without "to have": у меня есть
explanation: "I have a book" = "by me there-is a book": у + genitive of possessor + есть + thing in the nominative.
bridge_note: Russian kept the older Indo-European be-possessive/locative pattern (location-derived possession), reinforced in East Slavic.
mistake: seeking a verb "to have"; putting the possessed thing in the accusative.
branch: The Bones of the Simple Sentence: Gender, "to be", and "to have"

title: Negated existence/possession: нет + genitive
explanation: Absence uses нет + the genitive.
bridge_note: the "genitive of negation" marks the thing as removed from the set of existing things.
mistake: keeping the noun nominative after нет.
branch: The Bones of the Simple Sentence: Gender, "to be", and "to have"

title: What case is, and why endings replace word order
explanation: Russian marks a noun's role by changing its ending, freeing word order.
bridge_note: English lost case (keeping I/me, he/him); Russian kept the Proto-Slavic system minus the vocative.
mistake: the cardinal English error — ignoring endings, reading by position.
branch: Case System Fundamentals: The First Three Cases

title: Nominative case
explanation: The subject and the predicate noun after zero-copula.
mistake: forgetting the predicate noun stays nominative.
branch: Case System Fundamentals: The First Three Cases

title: Accusative singular: direct object + animacy rule
explanation: Inanimate m/n look like nominative; f -а→-у, -я→-ю; animate masculine takes the genitive-looking ending.
bridge_note: the animate-accusative-copies-genitive pattern keeps subject and object distinct after m nom/acc merged.
mistake: not marking feminine objects; ignoring animacy.
branch: Case System Fundamentals: The First Three Cases

title: Accusative of direction: в/на + accusative
explanation: Motion "to/into" uses в/на + accusative (Куда?).
bridge_note: the accusative marks the endpoint of motion.
branch: Case System Fundamentals: The First Three Cases

title: Prepositional case: location (в/на) and topic (о)
explanation: Never appears without a preposition; -е default. Answers Где? and "about what?".
bridge_note: shrunken descendant of the Proto-Slavic locative.
branch: Case System Fundamentals: The First Three Cases

title: в vs на for place
explanation: в = "in/at" (enclosed); на = "on/at" (surfaces, certain institutions/events: на почте, на концерте).
bridge_note: на collocations are partly lexicalized.
branch: Case System Fundamentals: The First Three Cases

title: Personal pronouns and declension
explanation: я, ты, он/она/оно, мы, вы, они decline (меня, мне, мной...); third-person forms add н- after prepositions (у него, с ней).
bridge_note: н- is a fragment of old prepositions ending in -n.
branch: Pronoun System

title: Possessive pronouns: agreement
explanation: мой/твой/наш/ваш agree with the thing possessed; его/её/их invariable.

examples.native: моя книга, моё окно, мой стол

mistake: making его/её agree; failing to decline мой.
branch: Pronoun System

title: Demonstrative этот/тот, determinative весь/каждый
explanation: этот agrees with its noun ("this"); это is invariable ("this is..."); весь/каждый mark "all/every".

examples.native: этот дом, эта книга, эти люди

mistake: confusing это ("this is...", invariable) with этот (agreeing).
branch: Pronoun System

title: Interrogatives кто/что/какой/чей/сколько
explanation: Question words that ask who, what, which, whose, and how many — кто and что decline like nouns through all six cases.

examples.native: Чья это книга? Какой сегодня день?

branch: Pronoun System

title: Relative который
explanation: Agrees in gender/number with its antecedent but takes case from its role in the relative clause.
bridge_note: the everyday spoken alternative to participles.
branch: Pronoun System

title: Reflexive себя and possessive свой
explanation: себя = "-self" for any person; свой = "one's own", pointing back to the subject.
bridge_note: свой disambiguates possessor identity.
mistake: using его/её where свой is required.
branch: Pronoun System

title: Negative pronouns никто/ничто and the double negative
explanation: Russian requires не on the verb even with никто.
bridge_note: Slavic negative concord.
branch: Pronoun System

title: Genitive singular
explanation: -а/-я (m/n), -ы/-и (f). Uses: "X of Y" (центр города), absence (нет времени), origin из/с, possessor у, after numbers 2+.
mistake: not using it after нет and numbers.
branch: The Rest of the Case System (Singular)

title: Dative singular
explanation: -у/-ю (m/n), -е (f). Uses: indirect object (звоню отцу), age (Ему двадцать лет), necessity (Мне надо...), motion к + dative.
bridge_note: the dative is the experiencer/beneficiary case — age and necessity happen to you, with no nominative subject.
branch: The Rest of the Case System (Singular)

title: Instrumental singular
explanation: -ом/-ем (m/n), -ой/-ей (f), special -ью for -ь feminines (ночью). Uses: instrument (пишу ручкой), accompaniment с + instr (с братом), profession (работает врачом), predicate after быть past/future (Он был студентом).
bridge_note: instrumental predicate signals a temporary/role state vs permanent identity.
mistake: using с for a plain instrument; leaving the predicate nominative after был.
branch: The Rest of the Case System (Singular)

title: Case after common prepositions (consolidation)
explanation: Fixed government — из/с/от/у/до/без + gen; к + dat; про/через/в/на(dir) + acc; с/над/под/за/между + instr; в/на(loc)/о/при + prep.

examples.native: из дома, к другу, с братом
examples.gloss: from home (genitive), to a friend (dative), with a brother (instrumental) — each preposition fixes its own case

mistake: wrong case per preposition. [Wade: prepositional government is a major problem area.]
branch: The Rest of the Case System (Singular)

title: Long-form agreement in the nominative
explanation: -ый/-ий/-ой (m), -ая/-яя (f), -ое/-ее (n), -ые/-ие (pl).

examples.native: новый дом, новая книга, новое окно

branch: Adjectives: Agreement, Declension, and Comparison

title: The spelling rules (7-letter / 5-letter)
explanation: After г,к,х,ж,ч,ш,щ write и not ы; after ж,ч,ш,щ,ц write е not unstressed о.
mistake: mechanical ending application without the filter.
branch: Adjectives: Agreement, Declension, and Comparison

title: Full adjective declension across all six cases
explanation: Adjectives take pronominal endings harmonizing with the noun's case.

examples.native: в новом доме, с новой книгой

mistake: declining the noun but not the adjective.
branch: Adjectives: Agreement, Declension, and Comparison

title: Hard-stem vs soft-stem adjectives
explanation: Soft-stem (синий, последний) shift the ending series into soft vowels.
branch: Adjectives: Agreement, Declension, and Comparison

title: Short-form adjectives
explanation: Predicate-only forms (рад, занят, болен, готов, должен at A1; productively at B1) expressing a temporary state, sometimes differing in meaning from the long form.
bridge_note: short forms are the older predicative adjective; long forms fused a demonstrative onto them.
branch: Adjectives: Agreement, Declension, and Comparison

title: Comparative degree
explanation: Synthetic (-ее/-е with mutation: интереснее, дороже, лучше) or compound более + adj; "than" = чем or bare genitive.

examples.native: Он умнее, чем я / умнее меня

mistake: doubling (более интереснее); forgetting mutations (к→ч, г→ж, х→ш).
branch: Adjectives: Agreement, Declension, and Comparison

title: Superlative degree
explanation: самый + adj (самый интересный) or synthetic -ейший/-айший (literary).
mistake: combining самый with a synthetic comparative.
branch: Adjectives: Agreement, Declension, and Comparison

title: Nominative plural of nouns
explanation: -ы/-и (most m/f), -а/-я (n and some m: города, дома), plus irregulars (друзья, братья, дети, люди).
branch: Plural Formation and the Plural Case System

title: Genitive plural — the hardest ending set
explanation: Masculine consonant stems add -ов/-ев (столов); feminines/neuters often take a zero ending with a fleeting vowel (девушка→девушек, окно→окон, сестра→сестёр).

examples.native: пять столов, много книг, мало окон

bridge_note: the zero ending is inherited from Proto-Slavic; the inserted vowel breaks the consonant cluster.
mistake: defaulting to one ending; missing the fleeting vowel.
branch: Plural Formation and the Plural Case System

title: Dative/instrumental/prepositional plural (-ам/-ами/-ах)
explanation: Uniform across genders — dat -ам/-ям, instr -ами/-ями, prep -ах/-ях (irregular людьми, детьми).

examples.native: к друзьям, с друзьями, о друзьях

bridge_note: the plural oblique cases levelled to a single set early.
branch: Plural Formation and the Plural Case System

title: Accusative plural and animacy
explanation: Animate plural = genitive plural; inanimate plural = nominative plural, across all genders.
mistake: not extending animacy to the plural.
branch: Plural Formation and the Plural Case System

title: Adjective/pronoun agreement in the plural
explanation: Adjectives and pronouns modifying a plural noun all take the plural's case ending, across all six cases.

examples.native: новые дома, в новых домах, моих друзей

branch: Plural Formation and the Plural Case System

title: Present tense: first conjugation (-е-/-ё-)
explanation: читать→читаю, читаешь, читает, читаем, читаете, читают.
mistake: keeping the infinitive stem unchanged; dropping person endings.
branch: Verb Conjugation and the Tense System

title: Present tense: second conjugation (-и-)
explanation: говорить→говорю, говоришь... говорят.
branch: Verb Conjugation and the Tense System

title: Consonant mutations in conjugation
explanation: Stem consonants alternate, esp. 1sg of 2nd conj (любить→люблю, видеть→вижу, писать→пишу).
bridge_note: fossilized ancient palatalization before a front vowel/j.
branch: Verb Conjugation and the Tense System

title: The verb classes/groups (1–14)
explanation: The standard organizes verbs into productive classes; learning the class predicts the paradigm.

examples.gloss: to read, to speak, to give — each belongs to one of 14 standard conjugation classes

branch: Verb Conjugation and the Tense System

title: -овать/-евать verbs
explanation: -ова-/-ева- becomes -у- in the present (советовать→советую).

examples.gloss: to advise → I advise (-ова- becomes -у- in the present)

branch: Verb Conjugation and the Tense System

title: Past tense: the -л participle
explanation: Past agrees in gender and number, not person: -л/-ла/-ло/-ли.

examples.native: Он читал, она читала, они читали

bridge_note: the modern past is historically a participle (old perfect with dropped auxiliary).
branch: Verb Conjugation and the Tense System

title: Compound (imperfective) future: буду + infinitive
explanation: Future of imperfectives = conjugated быть + imperfective infinitive.
branch: Verb Conjugation and the Tense System

title: High-frequency irregular/athematic verbs
explanation: хотеть (mixed), есть/дать (athematic), мочь, идти, ехать, жить, брать.

examples.native: я хочу, ты хочешь... они хотят

branch: Verb Conjugation and the Tense System

title: The imperative mood
explanation: From the present stem: -й/-и/-ь (читай(те), говори(те), будь(те)).
branch: Verb Conjugation and the Tense System

title: Verb government (глагольное управление)
explanation: Verbs fix the case of their complement (заниматься + instr, помогать + dat, ждать + gen/acc).
branch: Verb Conjugation and the Tense System

title: The core opposition
explanation: Imperfective = ongoing/habitual/general; perfective = a single completed whole with a result.
bridge_note: aspect is grammaticalized from Proto-Slavic; Slavic rebuilt its verb around aspect after losing older tense oppositions.
branch: Verbal Aspect: The Central Organizing Feature

title: Aspect pairs and formation
explanation: Pairs differ by prefix (писать→написать), suffix (-ыва-/-ива-: рассказать→рассказывать), or suppletion (говорить→сказать, брать→взять).
bridge_note: -ыва-/-ива- "re-imperfectivizes" a prefixed perfective (secondary imperfective).
mistake: assuming a prefix only adds meaning.
branch: Verbal Aspect: The Central Organizing Feature

title: Perfective future (the "present-form" future)
explanation: A perfective verb with present-tense endings = future.
bridge_note: perfectives can't denote present ongoing action, so their "present" forms became future.
mistake: буду + perfective; thinking prochitáyu is present.
branch: Verbal Aspect: The Central Organizing Feature

title: Aspect in the past
explanation: Imperfective past narrates an ongoing/repeated action; perfective past reports a single completed event with a result.
branch: Verbal Aspect: The Central Organizing Feature

title: Aspect in the imperative
explanation: Perfective for a specific one-off request (Прочитай это!); imperfective for general instructions, invitations, and (with negation) prohibitions (Не читай это!).
bridge_note: negated imperfective = "don't do"; negated perfective = "be careful not to accidentally".
mistake: negated perfective accidentally warning of danger (Не упади! = "don't fall!").
branch: Verbal Aspect: The Central Organizing Feature

title: Aspect in the infinitive (phase/modal verbs)
explanation: начать/кончать/продолжать take imperfective; забыть/успеть/удаться take perfective.
branch: Verbal Aspect: The Central Organizing Feature

title: Aspect with negation, and in the subjunctive
explanation: B2 requires aspect choice in all moods including the subjunctive and under negation. Example: Не надо было это делать. [B2 Std: "употребление видовых форм в изъявительном, повелительном, сослагательном наклонении... с отрицанием".]

examples.gloss: One shouldn't have done that. (aspect choice matters even under negation)

branch: Verbal Aspect: The Central Organizing Feature

title: Unidirectional vs multidirectional pairs
explanation: идти (one direction, now) vs ходить (repeatedly/around/there-and-back); ехать vs ездить (by vehicle).

examples.native: Я хожу в кино каждую неделю

bridge_note: Russian grammaticalized a directionality distinction English leaves to context.
mistake: the signature error — confusing pair members; идти for habitual motion.
branch: Verbs of Motion

title: Foot vs vehicle distinction
explanation: идти/ходить (on foot) vs ехать/ездить (by transport); also нести/носить, вести/водить, лететь/летать, плыть/плавать.
branch: Verbs of Motion

title: Prefixed motion verbs (по-, при-, у-, в-, вы-, пере-, до-, за-, под-, от-)
explanation: Prefixes add spatial meaning and aspect: по- makes a perfective "set off" (пойти, поехать); при-/у- = arrive/leave; в-/вы- = enter/exit. The multidirectional stem becomes imperfective, the unidirectional becomes perfective (приходить/прийти).
bridge_note: a spatial prefix bounds the motion, making it perfective, which then needs a re-derived imperfective.
branch: Verbs of Motion

title: Figurative/idiomatic motion verbs
explanation: время идёт, дождь идёт, речь идёт о.

examples.gloss: Time goes by / passes. It's raining. (literally: "rain goes/walks")

branch: Verbs of Motion

title: Cardinal 1–10 and the counting-case rule
explanation: 1 agrees like an adjective (один стол, одна книга); 2, 3, 4 → genitive singular (два стола, три книги); 5+ → genitive plural (пять столов).

examples.native: одна минута, две минуты, пять минут

bridge_note: 2 historically took the dual (now lost), 3–4 a plural merged with the genitive singular; 5+ were nouns ("a fiver of tables") governing the genitive plural — the 4-vs-5 "barrier".
mistake: nominative plural after 2–4 (the English instinct); genitive singular after 5+.
branch: Numerals and Quantity

title: Compound numerals and the "last digit" rule
explanation: The noun's case follows the last word (21 → 1-rule: двадцать один стол; 22 → 2-rule: двадцать два стола).
mistake: keying off the whole number's size.
branch: Numerals and Quantity

title: Ordinal numerals
explanation: Decline like adjectives (первый, второй, пятый); used for dates.

examples.native: первое января, в две тысячи двадцатом году

mistake: not declining; confusing cardinal/ordinal in dates.
branch: Numerals and Quantity

title: Declension of cardinal numerals
explanation: Numerals themselves decline (пяти, пятью; both parts of compound numbers decline).

examples.native: с пятью рублями; о двухстах студентах

mistake: leaving numerals undeclined in oblique cases. [Wade flags numeral declension as a notorious problem area.]
branch: Numerals and Quantity

title: Collective numerals (двое, трое, четверо)
explanation: Used with groups of people, male groups, pluralia tantum, "children".
branch: Numerals and Quantity

title: Time, age, dates, quantity words
explanation: Age → dative (Мне двадцать лет); много/мало/несколько + genitive plural.
branch: Numerals and Quantity

title: The concept of the participle (причастие)
explanation: A verb form behaving like an adjective, agreeing in gender/number/case while keeping the verb's aspect and government. Four types: active present, active past, passive present, passive past.

examples.gloss: reading (active present), who read (active past), being read (passive present), having been read (passive past)

bridge_note: participles are the written language's compression device; speech prefers который. [Std B1: "Понятие о причастии"; B2: "Причастие, причастный оборот".]
mistake: expecting them in speech (they are bookish).
branch: Participles and Gerunds (Verbal Adverbs)

title: Active present participle (-ущ-/-ющ-/-ащ-/-ящ-)
explanation: "The one who is doing X"; from the 3pl present stem.
branch: Participles and Gerunds (Verbal Adverbs)

title: Active past participle (-вш-/-ш-)
explanation: "The one who did X"; either aspect.
branch: Participles and Gerunds (Verbal Adverbs)

title: Passive present participle (-ем-/-им-)
explanation: "Being X-ed"; from imperfective transitives.
branch: Participles and Gerunds (Verbal Adverbs)

title: Passive past participle (-нн-/-енн-/-т-) — long and short
explanation: "Having been X-ed"; the short form is very common as a predicate and forms the passive. Examples (long): прочитанная книга; (short): Книга прочитана. Дом построен в 1990 году.

examples.gloss: the book that was read (long form) / The book is read. (short-form predicate)

bridge_note: short passive participle + (был/будет) is the normal analytic passive for perfective verbs.
mistake: -н-/-нн- spelling; leaving the short form unagreed.
branch: Participles and Gerunds (Verbal Adverbs)

title: The passive voice and active↔passive transformation
explanation: Two passives — the -ся passive (imperfective: Дом строится) and the short past passive participle (perfective: Дом построен), with the agent in the instrumental (построен рабочими).
mistake: agent in nominative; wrong passive per aspect. [B2 Std §2.3.7: "Правила трансформации действительных и страдательных конструкций".]
branch: Participles and Gerunds (Verbal Adverbs)

title: The gerund/verbal adverb (деепричастие)
explanation: Indeclinable, "while/having done X", sharing its subject with the main verb. Imperfective -я/-а (simultaneous: Читая, он улыбался); perfective -в/-вши (prior: Прочитав письмо, она заплакала).
bridge_note: the shared-subject rule is strict; violating it is a recognized error.
mistake: the classic dangling error (Подъезжая к станции, у меня слетела шляпа is famously wrong).
branch: Participles and Gerunds (Verbal Adverbs)

title: Transforming participial/gerund phrases ↔ clauses
explanation: Converting причастный оборот to a который-clause and деепричастный оборот to an adverbial clause — required for B2 writing, essential for C1 stylistic control. Example: Студент, сдавший экзамен ↔ Студент, который сдал экзамен.

examples.native: Студент, сдавший экзамен ↔ Студент, который сдал экзамен.
examples.gloss: The student who passed the exam (participle phrase ↔ который-clause, same meaning)

mistake: comma errors; aspect drift. [B2 §2.3.7 lists exactly these transformations.]
branch: Participles and Gerunds (Verbal Adverbs)

title: Subordinating conjunctions (cause, time, concession, result)
explanation: потому что/так как (cause), когда/пока/после того как/прежде чем (time), хотя/несмотря на то что (concession), поэтому/так что (result). B2 adds благодаря тому что, из-за того что, по мере того как.

examples.native: Я остался дома, потому что шёл дождь

mistake: comma placement; mixing что/чтобы. [B1 vs B2 inventories per Std.]
branch: Complex Sentences, Mood, and Reported Speech

title: что vs чтобы
explanation: что = "that" (fact, indicative); чтобы = "in order to / so that" (purpose/desire, + infinitive or + past-form verb).
bridge_note: чтобы contains бы and demands the irrealis past-form verb.
branch: Complex Sentences, Mood, and Reported Speech

title: The conditional/subjunctive mood with бы
explanation: Past-tense verb + invariable бы = hypothetical/counterfactual and polite wishes; real conditions use если + future, unreal use если бы + past + past+бы.

examples.native: Если бы я знал, я бы сказал

bridge_note: Russian has no morphological conditional — it recycles the past tense plus бы (a reduced old aorist of быть). [B2 Std names сослагательное наклонение and adds бы to the particle set.]
mistake: conjugating a special conditional; future after если бы.
branch: Complex Sentences, Mood, and Reported Speech

title: Reported (indirect) speech
explanation: Unlike English, Russian keeps the original tense; statements → что, commands → чтобы, questions → ли or the question word.

examples.gloss: lit. "he said that he will come"

bridge_note: Russian reports from the original speaker's vantage — no sequence-of-tenses shift. [B1 §2.3.4: "Правила перевода прямой речи в косвенную".]
branch: Complex Sentences, Mood, and Reported Speech

title: Neutral SVO and why order is "free but not random"
explanation: Because case marks roles, constituents reorder; neutral order is SVO but any order is grammatical.
branch: Word Order, Information Structure, and Register

title: Theme–rheme / given–new: the focus goes last
explanation: Known info (тема) first; new/important info (рема) last, carrying logical stress.

examples.gloss: "where the books are is the table"

bridge_note: with no articles, Russian uses position to mark a/the and old/new. [Prague-school/FSP analysis; exact level is JC.]
mistake: front-loading new info as in English.
branch: Word Order, Information Structure, and Register

title: Focus/emphatic particles (же, ведь, -то, даже, именно, только)
explanation: Tag a constituent as contrastive/salient; depend on placement.

examples.native: Я же говорил! Именно он это сделал

branch: Word Order, Information Structure, and Register

title: Negation scope with не
explanation: не immediately precedes the word it negates, changing meaning by position.

examples.native: Я не читаю книгу / Не я читаю книгу / Я читаю не книгу

branch: Word Order, Information Structure, and Register

title: Register: ты vs вы and politeness
explanation: ты (informal singular) vs вы (formal or plural); the choice signals social distance and is obligatory.
bridge_note: вы-politeness is a European convention layered onto the true plural.
branch: Word Order, Information Structure, and Register

title: Functional-stylistic register (colloquial vs neutral vs bookish/official)
explanation: B2 requires matching grammar to register — nominal style and stock verb-noun collocations in scientific/journalistic/official texts, participles/gerunds for formal writing.

examples.gloss: I hereby inform you... (bookish/official) vs Listen, basically... (colloquial) — same content, different register

mistake: bookish participles in casual speech; slang in formal writing. [B2 Std §2.3.8: "Функционально-стилистическое употребление".]
branch: Word Order, Information Structure, and Register
